reason: The hypothesis relies on a direct link between chemical homogenization and a narrowed exchange distribution, but the cited evidence (E3) only shows this effect for a different material system (Pd-added alloys) and does not confirm the mechanism in the FeMnNiGeSi HEA. E1 and E2 discuss magnetocaloric properties in other contexts but provide no support for the key premises about as-deposited disorder or the effect of annealing on hysteresis in this specific alloy.
premises: As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi HEA has significant local compositional fluctuations causing a broad distribution of magnetic exchange interactions.
This broad exchange distribution causes a broad and hysteretic magnetocaloric transition.
Low-temperature annealing reduces local chemical inhomogeneities in this HEA.
Reducing chemical inhomogeneities narrows the exchange distribution, sharpening the magnetocaloric response and reducing hysteresis.
